weighing 2152 g
one of monochorionic diamniotic twins
her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks

severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes

concepts.why: Fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI showed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement with severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes.
Funduscopic examination revealed mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign and very weak light reflexes bilaterally.
Fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI showed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement, which are associated with periventricular leukomalacia.
The infant was born with low birth weight and had a twin who died in utero, which are risk factors for intrauterine growth restriction.
Fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI showed ventricular enlargement, which is a characteristic of congenital hydrocephalus.
The infant was born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation, which is considered premature.
Fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI showed microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, which are indicative of cerebral dysgenesis.
Fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI showed microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, which are associated with neonatal encephalopathy.
It explains the preservation of certain brain structures despite significant abnormalities in others, as seen in the imaging findings.
It explains the mild optic nerve pallor and suspected peripapillary double-ring sign observed in the funduscopic examination.
